assignments.reason: The essential nature of this node is the act of prayer that constructs the Ani vessel — connecting machshava (thought/yud) to dibur (speech/nun) to complete the aleph-nun-yud formation. It belongs to the prayer-vessel domain, not to the hidden/revealed structural frame or any other package. It IS the process of forming the kli.

This node IS the completed Ani vessel — 'the vessel is formed'. Its essential nature is the kli/Ani itself, the receiving vessel for divine shefa. It is the culmination of the letter-formation process that defines Package 1. The word 'kli' here is an alias for 'Ani' (as noted in the additions analysis), placing it squarely in the Ani-vessel domain.

The essential nature of this node is machshava (thought) being connected to dibur (speech) — it is the yud-component of the Ani vessel in its active state. Machshava and dibur are both core nodes of Package 1, and this phrase describes their union, which IS the formation of the yud-letter within the kli. Its nature is inseparable from the prayer-vessel letter-structure.

This node IS the letter Yud being formed — the third letter of the word Ani. Its essential nature is the yud/machshava component of the prayer-vessel. The Yud is already a core node of Package 1 (machshava = yud per the bechina chain), and this phrase refers to the same letter completing its formation within the Ani vessel.

assignments.node_id: בתפלה לשמה, שיקשר המחשבה אל הדבור של התפלה, בקשר אמיץ וחזק
assignments.reason: The essential nature of this node is tefila lishmah — prayer for its own sake, with thought firmly bound to speech. This IS the method of constructing the Ani vessel. Its core components (machshava, dibur, tefila, kishur) all belong to the prayer-vessel domain. The qualifier 'lishmah' and 'b'kesher amitz v'chazak' specify the quality of the prayer but do not change its essential nature as the vessel-forming act of Package 1.

The essential nature of this node is reaching the nistar (the hidden) — accessing the penimit (inner dimension). The nistar/penimit IS the core concept of Package 2, which defines the hidden/revealed structural duality. This node belongs to the domain of what is sought (the hidden inner reality), not to the domain of how it is sought (the prayer-vessel). Its polarity is neutral because the hidden/revealed distinction is a cosmic structural feature applying equally to both Torah and God, as stated in the opening of the teaching.
